name: workspace
//: Depends on every other project so the cross-cutting checks run whenever anything they check can change. Without these edges a crate-only change would skip the graph check that keeps affected selection honest. llmlint: ignore-file[expensive_tests_stay_behind_their_own_edge,external_service_suite_stays_out_of_the_affected_tier] JSON has no comment to scope these to the `test` and `coverage` targets below, which are what they are about. The clone-based checks under `test` are cross-cutting by construction: what each drives — the git hooks, the gate's provisioning, the Nx graph itself, the plugin-isolation rule — is owned by no product project, so there is no narrower project to put them behind, and the edges above are exactly what makes them run when anything they check changes. `coverage` depends on every crate's coverage target, the two hosted plugins' included, because the 95% line floor is enforced once over the union of every crate's instrumented run; a coverage run cannot reach either service, because scripts/rust-coverage.sh clears GH_PROJECTS_TOKEN, LINEAR_API_KEY and ONETASKGRAPH_LIVE_REQUIRED before the run, so those suites skip their live journeys under it — scripts/check-live-lane.sh holds that clearing.

bootstrap.//: Uncached: it installs toolchain components and activates the git hooks path, both outside the tree.

options.command: bun run biome format --write nx.json biome.json package.json .claude workspace crates sdks

format.//: Uncached: it rewrites the tree in place.

options.command: bun run biome format nx.json biome.json package.json .claude workspace crates sdks

commands: bun run biome lint --error-on-warnings nx.json biome.json package.json .claude workspace crates sdks

typecheck.//: The SDK and script sources are inputs because check-workspace-config.sh scans them for the files that resolve target/debug/onetaskgraph and for a cargo invocation inside one; without them a spawner added to a test would not re-run this check.

test.//: Uncached: three checks clone a repository and read git history, which no input glob in this tree describes — a cached pass would assert about a graph that has since changed. Serial because those checks each clone into a scratch tree and run cargo or Nx there; racing them would contend for the same registry lock for no gain. The isolation concurrency check creates its own intentional fan-out inside that serial target. check-hook-safety runs first and takes milliseconds: it proves the scratch-clone helper the three later cloning checks depend on still survives the environment a git hook gives it, and if that has broken, their results below are about the wrong repository. check-pre-push-provisioning drives the real hook in an unprovisioned clone, which is what keeps a fresh worktree's missing toolchain from reading as a rejected push.

coverage-clear.//: Every crate's coverage target depends on this one, so Nx runs it once before the fan-out: it removes the raw profiles an earlier run left in target/llvm-cov-target and nothing else. A stale profile counts lines a since-changed binary no longer runs, and no crate can clear only its own because cargo-llvm-cov names every profile after the workspace. Uncached: its whole effect is on a directory no input describes.

coverage.//: The one place the Rust line floor is enforced: the report over the union of every crate's instrumented run, all of which this target depends on by name — scripts/check-coverage-enforced.sh reconciles that list against the crates in the tree, both ways, so a crate cannot fall out of the union in silence. Uncached because what it reads is the profile directory those runs just wrote, which no input glob describes. That dependency is what makes every crate's coverage run whenever this project is affected, which is whenever anything is; AGENTS.md records why that cost was accepted with the shared target directory.

commands: cargo deny check bans licenses sources

deny.//: Uncached: `cargo deny check advisories` fetches the RustSec advisory database, so a clean tree can start failing without a single file changing — which is the point of running it.
